↳ Posted by slainte on October 25th, 2004.

A rockin’ alternate version

Jeremy caught a funky version of this which I submitted as a ‘Ril Gan Ainm’… This is my attempt at a translation of Loretto Reid’s (Sligo transplant living in Canada) mad whistle playing… Keep in mind that, even after breaking my back to work out this version, nothing compares to Reid’s amazing and unique style and she never plays the same thing twice. Check out this tune and other great stuff with hubbie Brian Taheny on strings on ‘Celtic Mettle’ et. al….

T: The Fox on the Town
C: Trad (arr. Loretto Reid)
M: 4/4
L: 1/8
K: Gmaj

Re: The Fox On The Town

Just to correct the misinformation above, Finbarr, God rest him, was Richard’s brother (not his Father, the Father’s name was John).
As stated above by kkrell and as told to us in Kenmare by the composer himself(Richard!),Richard does not have a name on this tune but titles it simply as “Richard Dwyers”. He does not know either where the title “The Fox on The Town” originated from.

The Fox On The Town, X:10

We used to play this marvellous tune very often in sessions during tge 1980s and early 1990s. I remember we started in the low octave (played once) and played the rest in the high one. I’m not quite sure about the melody then - have no recording or written music - so I transcribed a lovely version by Brendan Mulholland and Paul McSherry that I found on YouTube which doesn’t seem be far away from ours:
https://youtu.be/VkFK7qB2Zxw
